title: The Fearful Traversing Murder Case
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Ran, Kogoro) omitted by convention. This episode interleaves two unrelated crimes: a professional hitman ('the Fox') hired by Bunzo Ushio to kill him, which turns out to be a decades-later revenge lure by Ushio against the Fox for killing his daughter in a botched hit six months earlier; and Akira Kawabe silencing his robbery accomplice Kyoko Saegusa. Only the Saegusa murder is modeled in full here, matching the v1 scope decision; the Fox/Ushio revenge plot and Ken'ichi Hirai's murder (committed by the Fox, disguised as the cabin manager, to protect his cover) are noted only as background context on the relevant person nodes, not modeled with their own motive/verb edges, to avoid conflating the two separate cases in one graph. The 'left-handed killer' theory pointing at novelist Shingo Nose is a genuine red herring the transcript spends real time developing before Conan overturns it with the fingernail-yarn evidence. case_type: murder.

attrs.claustrophobia: was once held captive in a cramped space by land sharks after refusing to sell his land, leaving him with severe claustrophobia; his panicked flight from the cabin during a landslide is what made him look suspicious, not guilt

attrs.note: a natural left-hander who trained himself to write right-handed (a 'switch-hitter'); wrongly accused by Kogoro of being the hitman 'the Fox' based on the knife angle in Saegusa's wound

persons.name: Bunzo Ushio
persons.occupation: president of a Kansai real estate agency branch

attrs.unrelated_subplot: hired the hitman 'the Fox' to kill him during this traverse, ostensibly after mistakenly believing he had terminal cancer; in truth this was a ploy to lure the Fox into the open in revenge for killing his young daughter Chisato in a botched contract hit six months earlier -- resolved as a separate case from Saegusa's murder

persons.name: Ken'ichi Hirai
persons.occupation: Tohto University hiking club member, regular at the mountain lodge

attrs.unrelated_subplot: killed by 'the Fox' (disguised as the mountain lodge's real manager) to protect his cover, after the Fox realized Hirai knew the real manager and would expose the impersonation -- part of the separate, unmodeled Ushio/Fox case

attrs.note: killed in a robbery at his home in Tanbara Village the morning of the traverse; 100 million yen was stolen from his safe

locations.name: Mountain lodge cabin near the summit

attrs.note: isolated overnight stop; phone line found deliberately cut, not storm-damaged as first assumed

attrs.wound_angle: diagonal, left-and-down -- initially read as proof of a left-handed killer, but Conan demonstrates the same angle is natural for a right-handed stab from behind if the victim wasn't wary of her attacker

attrs.amount: part of the 100 million yen stolen from Tanaka Yoro's safe
attrs.found_in: split between Saegusa's and Kawabe's packs; the blood matches the robbery victim, not Saegusa herself

attrs.forensic_trace: distinctively colored yarn scraps caught under Saegusa's fingernails match this sweater; she could only have been stabbed at close range by someone she wasn't wary of

clues.desc: The stab wound's diagonal left-down angle first seemed to prove the killer was left-handed, implicating the secretly left-handed novelist Shingo Nose -- but reenacting the stab shows the same angle works for a right-handed attacker striking from behind, so the angle alone doesn't identify the killer.
Yarn scraps caught under Saegusa's fingernails match the color of only one person's sweater at the cabin -- the one person she could have let get close enough to stab her without being on guard.

edges.detail: forced Tanaka Yoro to open his safe and stole 100 million yen from him
news reports describe both a man and woman forcing Tanaka to open his safe; the transcript does not specify which of them delivered the fatal blow
panics, believing Kogoro was sent to track them down over the Tanaka robbery-murder, and kills his own accomplice to keep her from turning herself (and him) in

edges.motive_type: concealment (silencing an accomplice he panicked into thinking would expose or endanger him)
